newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LME copper seen consolidating above $2,350 - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper seen consolidating above $2,350 - trade.

text.p: Three-month copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are expected to consolidate above the $2,350 level to find their next direction following a recent chart-based sell-off, Far East traders said on Thursday.
But a report that about 10,000 tonnes of copper is being shipped to Singapore from South Korea could put some pressure on the price recovery, they said.
"Copper prices are likely to trade in a short range between $2,350 to $2,400 following the sharp decline in prices," a trader at a local brokerage firm said.
Three-month copper prices rose to $2,375/$2,380 at 0700 GMT on Thursday in Asian trade from the the previous day's late LME close of $2,361/$2,366.

LME broker Macquarie said in its daily report that comments from BHP that it would have to cut back operations at its Ok Tedi mine, Papua New Guinea, if there was not sufficient rain by Friday provided little support.
It added there were rumours of at least 25,000 tonnes of copper coming into LME stocks in the next few weeks.

Indeed, with the backwardation still over $100 a tonne for cash to three-months, and demand moving into the seasonally slack (Northern Hemisphere) summer period, more material was likely to become available, it said.

The broker expected copper prices to trend lower in the second half of this year towards $1 a pound and to average 95 cents in 1998 with the market moving into modest oversupply in the second half of this year as smelter production increased, particularly at the U.S. Kennecott smelter.
Macquarie said if the three-month copper price falls below the 1997 uptrend line at $2,350 a tonne, a further heavy sell-off is likely.
Another LME broker, Brandeis, said technically prices have initially tested the uptrend line and the bottom of the up-channel which was evident at $2,355 a tonne and have successfully held.
Provided that this level can continue to hold and the market can consolidate in the $2,355-$2390 range, further serious weakness can be averted, it said.
Three-month aluminium bid prices also rose in tandem with copper to $1,570 at 0700 GMT in Asian trade from Wednesday's late LME close of $1,561.
Brandeis said the downside appeared to be accelerating and a close below $1,535/$1,540 would be very bearish. Resistance was seen at $1,570/$1,575.
